Crock Pot Hot Chocolate (Rich and Creamy Slow Cooker Recipe)

This post may contain affiliate links – please read my disclosure statement.

November 8, 2026November 8, 2026
Jump to Recipe
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 6:31
Instaread

I just made this slow cooker hot chocolate again tonight, and oh my goodness, I had forgotten how incredibly rich and creamy it is! My kids have been working so hard helping me with a big Elf on the Shelf project, and I thought they deserved a little break. What better way to reward them than with homemade hot chocolate and a Christmas movie?

I knew exactly which recipe I wanted to make—this one! Holly even asked how I made it, and the kids said it tasted like drinking melted chocolate straight from a cup. My husband had an even better description. He said, “This is how I imagine drinking Willy Wonka’s chocolate river would taste!” That pretty much sums it up. It’s wonderfully rich, creamy, and full of chocolate flavor.

This homemade hot chocolate is perfect for chilly winter evenings, snow days, warming up after building snowmen, Christmas parties, or setting up a holiday hot chocolate bar. And here’s something new I discovered tonight: although I usually make it in the slow cooker, I tried it on the stovetop this time. I simply warmed everything together, stirring until the chocolate melted and blended into the milk. It took about five minutes, and it was wonderful!

Why You’ll Love This Crockpot Hot Chocolate

  • This recipe is made with condensed milk, so it’s extra rich and creamy
  • It’s all put together in a snap, too. Just pour everything into the crockpot, stir once in a while and enjoy
  • The perfect recipe for holidays like Thanksgiving, or Christmas or drink it on cold fall and winter nights

Crockpot Hot Chocolate Ingredients

You’ll need five ingredients for this rich, creamy hot chocolate:

  • 6 cups milk: I like 2% milk, but whole milk works, too.
  • 14 ounces sweetened condensed milk: Adds sweetness and a creamy texture.
  • 2 cups milk chocolate chips: Semi-sweet chocolate chips are an option if you prefer.
  • 16 ounces heavy whipping cream: Makes the hot chocolate extra rich and creamy.
  • 1 teaspoon vanilla extract: I prefer pure vanilla, but imitation vanilla works.

Slow Cooker Hot Chocolate Recipe: Step-by-Step Instructions

  1. Add the milk, sweetened condensed milk, chocolate chips, heavy whipping cream, and vanilla extract to the slow cooker.
  2. Mix the ingredients together and place the lid on the slow cooker.
  3. Cook on low for 2 hours, stirring occasionally.

You’ll find the printable recipe card with all the measurements below.

Can You Make This Hot Chocolate on the Stovetop?

Yes! I tested this same recipe on the stovetop when I made it for my kids’ Christmas movie night. I warmed the ingredients together, stirring until the chocolate melted and everything blended smoothly. It took about five minutes. Use the slow cooker when you want to make hot chocolate for a gathering, or the stovetop when you want a quick batch at home.

Hot Chocolate Toppings and Serving Ideas

  • Whipped Cream
  • Marshmallows
  • Sprinkles – I love Wilton’s Turtle Crunch on Hot Chocolate
  • Hershey’s chocolate syrup
  • Chopped Peanuts
  • Cinnamon
  • Coconut Shavings
  • Squeeze Caramel Sauce

More Ways to Serve Your Hot Chocolate

  • Peppermint sticks
  • Candy Canes
  • Peppermint spoons
  • Chocolate spoons
  • Caramel
  • Cookies
  • Egg Nog
  • Mint
  • Milk Chocolate Chips
  • Semisweet Chocolate Chips
  • Toffee
  • Nuts
  • Wafer sticks
  • Kit-Kats – bite the ends off to drink the hot cocoa through
  • sea salt
  • for adults – Baileys Irish Cream

Melissa’s Tips for Creamy Crockpot Hot Chocolate

  • don’t forget to stir the hot chocolate occasionally, but you’ll want to resist doing it constantly. Every time you take the lid off of the slow cooker or crock pot it will lose a good amount of heat
  • you can mix the ingredients easily with a whisk to combine fully

Easy Crockpot Hot Chocolate for a Classroom Party

This slow cooker hot chocolate is a cozy option to consider for a classroom winter or Christmas party. The recipe makes approximately 10–12 servings. Check the classroom’s food-allergy rules and plan for adult handling of the hot slow cooker and serving cups.

Hot Chocolate for a Crowd

The recipe card makes about 10–12 servings, making this a practical hot chocolate for a small gathering. For a larger group, use the recipe card to adjust the servings and make sure the full batch will fit safely in your slow cooker.

Crockpot Hot Chocolate Recipe FAQs

Is crockpot hot cocoa the same as hot chocolate?

People often use the terms hot cocoa and hot chocolate interchangeably. This crockpot hot cocoa uses real chocolate chips, milk, sweetened condensed milk, and heavy cream for a rich, creamy drink.

Can I use semi-sweet chocolate chips for crockpot hot chocolate?

Yes. I use milk chocolate chips in this recipe, but you can substitute semi-sweet chocolate chips if you prefer. The chocolate flavor will be less sweet.

Can I make crockpot hot chocolate ahead of time?

Yes! This is a great make-ahead recipe. Just store the liquid in an airtight container in the refrigerator. Make sure to check the expiration date on the milk that you have used, and don’t store it beyond that date.

How long does homemade hot chocolate last?

Store leftover hot chocolate in a sealed container in the refrigerator and enjoy within 3–4 days. Refrigerate promptly after serving.

Reheating: You can reheat it on the warm setting in the slow cooker, on the stove top on low heat, or in individual cups in the microwave
